digest.component_or_area: Gerrit Verified CI/CD workflow - Ubuntu runner utilization and test latency optimization
propositions: Ubuntu Verified jobs occupy 30+ runner-minutes per change while macOS remains the completion critical path at 22-23 minutes, creating org-wide queue contention.
Repeated YAML parsing in bridge_schedule() 1,440-minute loop adds ~100-130 seconds per Ubuntu run; hoisting the schedule load eliminates redundant I/O while preserving exhaustive minute verification.

Pandoc hardening test executes 3,421 redundant legacy-renderer subprocesses (883 duplicates) while the immutable expected-output oracle suffices; eliminating the duplicate legacy subprocesses saves 18+ seconds without removing real-Pandoc coverage.

Static golden Pandoc fixtures plus small representative live-Pandoc contracts plus full corpus replay in External Integration lane can preserve ADR 0095 coverage boundaries while reducing per-change execution by moving full real-Pandoc replay out of the hot path.

Gerrit Verified run 31834896849 exceeded 57 minutes due to pre-cancellation-fix always() predicates preventing superseded job cancellation and blocking the replacement via same-change concurrency; Gerrit 1792 repair restores GitHub cancellation semantics.

Current post-remediation organic full routes average 25 minutes end-to-end with no individual pytest phase exceeding 30 seconds, achieving the 20-30 minute target and freeing 7m17s per Verified run (21.1% Ubuntu occupancy reduction baseline-normalized) while preserving every platform cell, selector, assertion, and coverage boundary.
